physical_sequence: Bot turns write-latch20–36, advancing the coral proposal on its visible rack.

shots.consequence: The opening configuration is visibly endangered, but the proposed roof is mechanically stopped before it can overwrite the empty anchors.

shots.narration: Every change should leave a trail.
physical_sequence: The falling teal eave strikes the visible discard-trip latch.
The latch releases an exposed paper leaf spring connected to the gold catch tongue and segmented history strip.
The driven tongue hooks the teal eave before the discard mouth; successive owned strip segments unfold and carry the roof into the original-state bay.

The tongue seats the original in the first gold bay and closes the discard mouth; a visible gold connecting strip attaches to the still-braked coral write rack without moving the coral roof. The comparison drive will move it only after checkpoint capture.

The house’s empty roof slots are the completed physical change from shot01. The retained teal roof records the prior seated state while the live house is visibly roofless. The uninstalled coral proposal is not claimed as a completed version.
shots.consequence: A retained original is physically linked to the pending replacement rack, allowing restoration before actual logged renovation.

quality.purpose: Record the ACTUAL COMPLETED CHANGE of removing the seated roof: live slots are empty and the previous teal-roof state is physically retained. The pending coral proposal is intentionally not a completed roof exchange.
quality.hero: The newly engaged gold archive catching the original roof and attaching its retained trail to the pending replacement rack.
quality.primary_action: Falling roof trips the newly engaged spring catch; original roof seats in its history bay, and gold trail attaches to the stationary pending replacement rack.
quality.before: The completed removal has left the live house roofless; the teal prior roof is falling toward discard, and the uninstalled coral proposal remains on its braked rack.
quality.after: The original teal roof is retained in the gold history bay; the terminal strip hooks the braked pending coral rack. Live roof slots remain empty, and the proposal remains stationary.
secondary_motion: History-strip segments open successively from the spring-owned inner segment to the outer bay.
The hooked teal roof overshoots its bay by four pixels and returns.
The discard mouth closes only after the original roof lands in its history bay; the proposed coral roof stays on its braked rack, attached to the newly visible connecting strip.

The roof descends40 author pixels into a frontmost cream-backed discard latch; the latch visibly depresses20 pixels before releasing the linked spring. The tongue approaches only after release, then follows the actual eave.

shots.narration: Let the agent test the result.
physical_sequence: Bot grips the raised rain-ribbon anchor and pulls the translucent strip at a same bounded eased stroke.
The existing rain pull8 opens the visible reservoir outlet and transfers the same slug to the connected guide. Its release and handoff are explicit before the roof contact.
One large teal test-water slug reaches the coral drainage notch, exits the roof edge and strikes the upper window flap.
The slug enters the house and impacts the floor at one unambiguous point.
A clipped teal wet mask spreads across the persistent floor strip, then the same strip bends into its finite asymmetric fourteen-pixel sag while Bot holds for recognition.
shots.consequence: The controlled test physically produces a wet, sagging interior floor that persists into rollback.

quality.purpose: Show one readable water path and a persistent physical failure at mobile size.
quality.hero: The coral-roof rowhouse, one large test-water slug and the deforming floor.
quality.primary_action: Bot pulls the test ribbon; its water slug traverses the roof notch and window before wetting and bending the floor.
quality.before: The coral roof is installed; the ribbon is raised and the floor is cream, level and dry. The floor is already supported by the persistent floor-shuttle; its wet-saddle stays attached as the floor wets and bends, so support continues into rollback.
quality.after: The test-water slug has entered the house; the actual floor strip is fully wet and held in its asymmetric sag state.

The water slug compresses only at the notch and window contacts.
The floor wet mask and sag stop at declared finite states; no global house shake is added.
The same visible floor-shuttle stays beneath the actual floor throughout wetting; support is not acquired invisibly at the following cut.
